newsitem.title: UK: Granada sceptical on digital terrestrial TV.
newsitem.headline: Granada sceptical on digital terrestrial TV.

text.p: Granada Group on Wednesday ruled out playing a leading role in the development of digital terrestrial television when it is launched in the UK in 1998.
"We can't see the killer application for this. We are very sceptical about it as a purely commercial proposition," chief executive Charles Allen said in a statement.

He said that the key drivers of pay television were films and sport, areas in which satellite broadcaster BSkyB has built up a very strong position. Granada has a stake of just over 10 percent in BSkyB.

Digital terrestrial television -- broadcast from land-based transmitters -- will offer some 35 channels. Invitations to apply to operate blocks of frequencies have just been issued but Allen made it clear Granada was unlikely to get involved.
BSkyB plans to launch digital satellite services late next year, offering up to 200 channels.
